chunks: He said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Shadhuwayh al-Muʻaddab narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Jaʻfar al-Himyari narrated to us from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Masʻada ibn Sadaqa, from al-Sadiq Jaʻfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:
No thing has been added to something that is more virtuous than forbearance added to knowledge.

key_terms.حِلْم: Hilm - Forbearance: the quality of self-restraint, patience, and gentleness, especially in the face of provocation or ignorance
key_terms.شُبَّ: Shubba - Was mixed/added: from the root sh-b-b, meaning to blend, combine, or join one quality with another
key_terms.عِلْم: ʿIlm - Knowledge: sacred and scholarly knowledge, encompassing both religious learning and intellectual understanding

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the relationship between knowledge and forbearance?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him), through a chain of narrators traced back through the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt, states that no quality enhances another more than forbearance (hilm) enhances knowledge (ʿilm). This teaching was delivered to emphasize the complementary nature of these two virtues in Islam: knowledge without forbearance can lead to arrogance, while forbearance without knowledge may lack direction. The original audience—the companions and followers of the Imams—understood this as a call to cultivate both scholarly learning and emotional restraint as inseparable components of true wisdom.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Shadhuwayh al-Mu’addab (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. `Abdullah b. Ja`far narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to me. He said: Harun b. Muslim narrated to me from Mas`ada b. Sadaqa from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (as). He said: Amir al-Mu’minin (as) said:
No thing has been added to something that is more virtuous than forbearance added to knowledge.
